# Test fixtures

Realistic Jellyfin responses for the in-process fake server of P2 (`src/api` tests) and later phases. Every file validates against the 12.4.0 OpenAPI schema it mirrors (checked 2026-11-08; see api-notes.md for what was verified where); every "*(verify in P2)*" item is also a fixture-vs-reality check when a real 12.4 server is in front of us — fix shapes here and in api-notes.md in the same commit when reality disagrees.

Files: `playback_start_request`, `playback_progress_request`, `playback_stopped_request`, `client_capabilities_request` (the bodies `playbackReportBody()` and `clientCapabilitiesBody()` must produce; each validates against its 12.4 schema), `playbackinfo_no_compatible` (what a 12.4 server returns when nothing is compatible: HTTP 200, every `Supports*` false, no `ErrorCode`; observed live), `device_profile_default` (golden `DeviceProfile` that `buildDeviceProfile({})` must produce, parity §3), `system_info_public` (`GET /System/Info/Public`, no auth), `authenticate_request` + `authenticate_success` (`POST /Users/AuthenticateByName`, includes `Policy.EnableContentDownloading` because the downloads UI gates on it), `user_views` (`GET /UserViews`; **object** with `Items`, `StartIndex`, `TotalRecordCount`), `playbackinfo_direct` + `playbackinfo_transcode` (`POST /Items/{itemId}/PlaybackInfo`, a direct-play mkv vs a DOVI 2160p source with an HLS `TranscodingUrl`), `episodes_page` (`GET /Shows/{seriesId}/Episodes`, one page out of 12 with `TotalRecordCount`), `movie_item` (`GET /Items`, a Movie with user data + media source), `media_segments` (`GET /MediaSegments/{itemId}`, Intro + Recap per the `MediaSegmentType` enum), `quick_connect_initiate` (`POST /QuickConnect/Initiate` returns user code and private secret), `quick_connect_pending` + `quick_connect_approved` (`GET /QuickConnect/Connect?secret=`, same secret with authorization false/true; successful exchange then returns `authenticate_success` from `POST /Users/AuthenticateWithQuickConnect`), `ws_*` frame shapes (WebSocket inbound messages per the approved P2a design in websocket-contract.md, **corrected in the same session to the live 12.4.0 captures**: `ws_force_keepalive` (`ForceKeepAlive`, `Data: 60`, the wire order `MessageId, Data, MessageType`), `ws_keepalive_reply` (the client's own `KeepAlive` echo shape, the exact reply bytes still unobserved — the server answers by keeping the connection), `ws_library_changed` (a scan delta with `FoldersAddedTo/FoldersRemovedFrom/ItemsAdded/ItemsRemoved/ItemsUpdated/CollectionFolders/IsEmpty`), `ws_user_data_changed` (**`UserId` + `UserDataList` rows with `ItemId`/`Key`/`PlayCount`/`Played`/`LastPlayedDate`/`PlaybackPositionTicks`/played-percentage fields** — the earlier-guessed `ItemsIdList` key does not exist on 12.4; the client also still accepts that older shape defensively), `ws_playstate` (`Command` + the optional `SeekPositionTicks` + `ControllingUserId`), `ws_general_command` (`Name` + `Arguments` + `ControllingUserId`), `ws_play` (**`PlayCommand`**, `ItemIds`, `ControllingUserId` — the `Command` key is not what 12.4 sends), `ws_sessions` (the admin-only broadcast array — 12.4 sends no `Sessions` frames to non-admin sockets), `ws_server_restarting`, `ws_user_deleted`; every shape here traces its live-capture sibling and the acceptance is still `test_contracts.py` parse-checked).

Conventions: uuid-free ids are fine except where a route needs the uuid format (ItemId fields); ticks are the usual 10 MHz 100-ns units; tags are opaque strings. Keep files small and named after the endpoint they describe.
